title: Reserve reading comprehension
instructions: Read the passage, then answer all five questions before submitting the protected form.

parts.prompt: Why did the committee count borrowed and returned bowls each evening?

options.text: To measure how well the return system was working
To decide which meals tasted best
To replace the washing points
To calculate the number of market visitors exactly

choice_rationales.A: The two counts allow a return rate to be assessed.
choice_rationales.D: One visitor could borrow more than once, so this would not be exact.

parts.hint: Protected reserve: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Comparing loans and returns measured the system's performance.

parts.prompt: In paragraph 2, what does “its location” refer to?

options.text: The location of the night market
The location of the washing point near the entrance
The location of every food stall
The location of the drinks menu

choice_rationales.A: The sentence discusses one return point.
choice_rationales.B: The pronoun refers to the nearest relevant singular washing point.
choice_rationales.D: The hidden menu detail appears later.

parts.hint: Protected reserve: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: “Its” refers to the washing point whose return rate was lower.

parts.prompt: What does “assumed” most nearly mean in paragraph 2?

options.text: accepted as true without enough evidence
proved through repeated measurement
announced to every customer
removed from consideration

choice_rationales.A: The volunteers formed an initial explanation before asking customers.
choice_rationales.D: They initially considered the location important.

parts.hint: Protected reserve: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Assumed means believed something without first establishing it.

parts.prompt: Which statement best expresses the main idea?

options.text: Deposits guarantee that every borrowed item is returned
Customer evidence helped the committee identify and test one practical improvement
Washing points should always be placed at market entrances
Reusable bowls are unsuitable for night markets

choice_rationales.A: Some bowls were still taken home.
choice_rationales.B: Interviews identified the hidden sign and a second trial tested the change.
choice_rationales.C: The issue was sign visibility, not a universal location rule.
choice_rationales.D: The committee improved rather than rejected the system.

parts.hint: Protected reserve: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The passage shows evidence replacing an assumption and guiding a measured change.

parts.prompt: Which inference is best supported by the final sentence?

options.text: The organisers recognised that more than one factor could affect bowl losses
The second week had no missing bowls
Customers refused to read all signs
The committee planned to end the trial immediately

choice_rationales.A: They say clear signs help but cannot prevent every loss.
choice_rationales.B: Some bowls were still taken home.
choice_rationales.C: The passage does not blame all customers.
choice_rationales.D: No plan to stop is reported.

parts.hint: Protected reserve: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The bounded claim shows that signage was helpful but not the only influence.
